correctness.rationale: PASS for the replacement, not the original unqualified claim that outside the windows neither orbit attracts. The original Finding says asymptotically attracting and excludes attraction at both endpoints, whereas its strict multiplier test makes no nonlinear determination there; the failure is lack of an established exclusion, not a claim here that an endpoint is attracting. Replacements restrict the exact classification to hyperbolic attraction and explicitly reserve nonlinear equality cases. The two-cycle equations force s=A sin(s)cos(d)=0 under |A|<1, and d=B sin(d) then gives a bijection with positive roots. Monotonic d cot d gives all lobes and the unique nondegenerate fold on each higher lobe. On p=0 the common one-step Jacobian has quadratic nonzero spectrum and its square is the return. Strict Schur inequalities reduce to Bc<1 at c>0 and ac>-1 at c<0; c=0 has nilpotent derivative. On the right half-lobe d cot d+A cos d decreases to minus infinity, giving the unique upper threshold. At the fold a return multiplier is +1 and at the exit the nonzero multipliers have unit modulus, so neither endpoint is hyperbolic. Taylor expansion of the fold and exit equations gives offsets 1/m+O(m^-3) and 2/m+O_A(m^-2) from the sine maximum and hence the required width. For high lobes the replacement's exact separation follows from R_k^2=r_k^2+(2-A sin w)^2, r_k<m_k+pi/2 and 9/(2m_k)<pi. The frozen numerical checker was inspected but not run; no finite test is used to infer the classification.
